transcript.text: Alright everyone, we're here to finalize the production rollout plan for the new offline-sync engine. As you know, it's scheduled for a Wednesday production rollout, and it's already passed the planned functional and staging reliability tests. Before I can record the rollout plan, I need final status from each of the required functions: mobile engineering, reliability, customer support, and privacy. Let's go around and get everyone's final status. Who wants to start?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: While reviewing a compatibility report for an unrelated mobile release this morning, I confirmed that Android versions below 8.5 emit the legacy tombstone format that the new sync engine cannot reconcile. The approved first-rollout audience therefore includes iOS and Android 8.5 or newer, while Android versions below 8.5 are excluded. I haven't updated the rollout document yet because the compatibility report was completed only this morning.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to share my reliability findings before we finalize this. During a traffic replay, I measured the production sync queue and confirmed that a rollout above 5 percent would exceed the queue's safe processing margin. I also confirmed that reliability needs a 30-minute observation period after enabling the flag. I haven't added these numbers to the release ticket yet, but they're critical for the rollout plan.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to share my customer support findings before we finalize. While preparing support coverage, I confirmed from current support cases that the Aurora and Helix enterprise accounts have active offline workflows and must be excluded from the first rollout until their account teams complete a separate acceptance check. I haven't posted the account list in the release channel yet.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: I need to share my privacy findings before we finalize this. In a privacy review I completed this afternoon, I confirmed that the sync payload can carry location metadata, and that the first rollout must disable location metadata for every user until the data-use review is closed. This finding isn't in the privacy tracking system yet because the review finished just minutes ago, but it's a blocker for the rollout plan: location metadata must be disabled for all users before we go to production.
transcript.speaker: A5
